images.title: Pieces that fill the circle
images.purpose: Show that 4 pieces of 1/4 and 8 pieces of 1/8 each fill one whole circle, so the bottom number is the number of pieces needed.
images.composition: Two whole circles side by side: one cut into 4 pieces each marked 1/4, one cut into 8 pieces each marked 1/8, with the count and the whole written below each.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two whole circles side by side, both with radius 230 px, centres at y 340, so each circle spans y 110 to 570. Thin dark #2B2B2B cut lines (3 px) and outline, the first cut line pointing straight up (12 o'clock). LEFT: the circle with centre x 390 (x 160 to 620) is cut by 4 radii into exactly 4 equal pieces of 90 degrees (the cut lines run straight up, right, down and left), every piece filled teal #0072B2. In the middle of each of the 4 pieces the label 1/4 in white bold sans-serif (48 px). RIGHT: the circle with centre x 1066 (x 836 to 1296) is cut by 8 radii into exactly 8 equal pieces of 45 degrees (the 4 straight cut lines plus 4 diagonal ones), every piece filled amber #E69F00. In the middle of each of the 8 pieces the label 1/8 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (38 px). Under the left circle, centred at x 390: the line 4 pieces of 1/4 at y 640 (40 px dark) and the line 4/4 = 1 whole at y 710 (60 px bold dark). Under the right circle, centred at x 1066: the line 8 pieces of 1/8 at y 640 (40 px) and the line 8/8 = 1 whole at y 710 (60 px bold). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a circle cut into a number of pieces other than 4 on the left and 8 on the right, or pieces of unequal size
images.takeaway: n pieces of 1/n fill the whole: 4 pieces of 1/4 and 8 pieces of 1/8 each make 1.
images.description: A circle cut into 4 equal pieces marked 1/4 and a circle cut into 8 equal pieces marked 1/8, with 4/4 = 1 whole and 8/8 = 1 whole written under them.
images.context: Concept image for Making a Whole with Pieces of One Size. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a round whole made of equal pieces each marked with its fraction) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 1/4 and 1/8.
images.teaching_notes: Count the pieces aloud and match the count to the bottom number. The slip to watch: thinking the bottom number counts only the pieces you take, not all the equal pieces of the whole.

image_decisions.why: The two circles of equal pieces make 'n pieces of 1/n make a whole' countable and let the student see why the bottom number is the piece count.
